cards.title: Core idea
cards.body: Data distribution is how a database spreads data across storage units or machines. It uses two independent techniques: partitioning (split the data) and replication (copy the data).

cards.title: How it works
cards.body: Partitioning splits by rows (horizontal) or columns (vertical); sharding is horizontal partitioning across servers, scaling storage and writes. Replication copies data to more servers for availability and read scaling. Strategies: range, list, hash or composite, chosen from access patterns; each shard is usually replicated.

questions.q: Does replication help a database handle more writes?
questions.a: Not with a single leader. Every replica applies every write, so replicas add reads and fault tolerance, not write capacity.
